newsitem.title: USA: BASEBALL-CARDINALS EDGE PADRES IN NL PLAYOFF OPENER.
newsitem.headline: BASEBALL-CARDINALS EDGE PADRES IN NL PLAYOFF OPENER.

text.p: Gary Gaetti's three-run homer in the first inning was all the firepower St Louis pitchers needed as the Cardinals held off the San Diego Padres 3-1 in the National League divisional playoff opener on Tuesday.
Todd Stottlemyre and two relievers combined on an eight-hitter with veteran closer Dennis Eckersley snuffing out a potential ninth-inning San Diego rally to seal the victory.

Game Two of the best-of-five series is set for Thursday in St Louis. The defending World Series champion Atlanta Braves host the Los Angeles Dodgers in Game One of the other NL playoff series on Wednesday.
Stottlemyre pitched for the World Series champion Toronto Blue Jays in 1992 and 1993, but notched his first post-season win Tuesday.
He silenced the Padres' bats for the first five innings, allowing only a one-out double to Tony Gwynn in the first inning and a walk to Ken Caminiti in the fourth.
Gaetti gave Stottlemyre three runs to work with in the first inning.

With two out, Padres starter Joey Hamilton hit Ron Gant with a pitch and gave up a Brian Jordan single to centre. Gaetti then ripped a 1-1 pitch over the right-centre field fence for a quick 3-0 lead.
Stottlemyre allowed a leadoff home run to Rickey Henderson in the sixth that made it 3-1.
But the St Louis ace left Gwynn and Wally Joyner stranded on base by striking out Chris Gomez to end the inning.
The Padres put two men on base again in the seventh, but Rick Honeycutt relieved Stottlemyre and got Gwynn to fly to left-centre, ending the threat.
Honeycutt allowed a single to Steve Finley and struck out Caminiti in the eighth when Cardinals manager Tony La Russa summoned Eckersley, who got pinch-hitter Greg Vaughn to pop out and fanned Gomez.
San Diego had one last gasp when Eckersley allowed two-out singles to pinch-hitter Chris Gwynn and Henderson in the ninth, bringing to bat future Hall of Famer Tony Gwynn with the tying runs on base.
Eckersley robbed Gwynn of a base hit when he snared a sharp comebacker to record his 12th career post-season save.
